extra.message: Unsafe pickle deserialization of attacker-controlled request body — Remote code execution on the API server [verified: pickle.loads is called directly on attacker-supplied body/query bytes with no type restriction; the only gate is a shared static token compared with `!=`, which does not neutralize the RCE once reached.]

OS command injection via unsanitized host parameter — Arbitrary OS command execution on the server [verified: `host` flows unsanitized into a shell string via os.system, allowing shell metacharacter injection (`; curl ...`) with no validation anywhere in the handler.]

Region scoping bypass for dispatcher accounts with unset region_id — A dispatcher account without an assigned region can view and manage jobs, incidents, routes, and exports across all regions instead of being restricted, breaking the region tenancy boundary [verified: user_region_allowed returns true for a dispatcher with region_id is None regardless of the target region, so any dispatcher account lacking a region assignment gets global cross-region access to jobs, incidents, routes, workers, and exports instead of default-deny.]

Path traversal in arbitrary file write plus plaintext PII storage — Arbitrary file write outside the intended export directory, plus plaintext exposure of SSN/card data at rest [verified: `ref` is interpolated directly into a filesystem path with no traversal sanitization, and PII (ssn/card) is written to disk in plaintext at that path.]

Unsafe eval() of user-controlled expression — Potential arbitrary code execution via eval sandbox escape [verified: eval() runs the raw `expr` query param; restricting only `__builtins__` is a well-known insufficient sandbox (attribute-chain gadgets like `().__class__.__mro__` remain reachable).]

Server-Side Template Injection via string-built Jinja template — Arbitrary code execution through Jinja2 sandbox escape gadgets [verified: `fragment` is string-concatenated into a Jinja2 Template and rendered, giving full SSTI via `{{ }}`/`{% %}` syntax with no sandboxing (plain jinja2.Template, not SandboxedEnvironment).]

Path traversal in file write endpoint via unsanitized filename — Arbitrary file write to attacker-chosen paths on the server filesystem [verified: `name` query param is used unsanitized as the write target under BASE_EXPORT_DIR, permitting path traversal to write attacker-controlled files anywhere reachable.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection in XML parsing endpoint — Read arbitrary files on the server or perform SSRF via crafted DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations [verified: XMLParser is explicitly configured with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True on attacker-controlled body content, enabling classic XXE file-read/SSRF via DOCTYPE/ENTITY.]

Password reset tokens persisted in plaintext to a log file regardless of environment — Account takeover: anyone able to read local_mocks/password_resets.log (backup process, log shipper, misconfigured static hosting, insider access) obtains valid unexpired reset tokens for arbitrary accounts and can reset their passwords. [verified: request_password_reset unconditionally writes the raw reset token to local_mocks/password_resets.log (main.py:506-508) regardless of APP_ENV, unlike the dev_reset_token response gated at line 512, exposing valid unexpired tokens to anyone with filesystem/log access.]

Password reset tokens written to disk in plaintext — Anyone with read access to the application filesystem/logs (e.g. via a separate LFI/backup exposure, misconfigured log shipping, or shared hosting) can recover valid, unexpired password-reset tokens and take over any account that requested a reset. [verified: Duplicate of idx 4: the plaintext token write to local_mocks/password_resets.log at main.py:506-508 runs unconditionally in every environment including production.]

Region-scoping bypass on dashboard for unset-region dispatchers — A dispatcher whose region_id is null sees job/incident counts and data across every region instead of being denied, leaking cross-region business data [verified: main.py:564 skips region filter entirely when dispatcher.region_id is None (elif condition simply false), returning all-region job/incident dashboard data with no other guard.]

Region-scoping bypass on job listing endpoint for unset-region dispatchers — Under-scoped dispatcher can enumerate and view job/customer data belonging to other regions [verified: main.py:660 same pattern on primary job listing endpoint; under-scoped dispatcher enumerates jobs/customers across all regions.]

Region-scoping bypass on route CSV export for unset-region dispatchers — Bulk cross-region export of customer PII and worker schedule data via CSV download [verified: main.py:1400 same pattern on route CSV export, enabling bulk cross-region export of PII/schedule data with no compensating check.]

Region-scoping bypass on completions CSV export for unset-region dispatchers — Bulk cross-region export of customer/job completion PII via CSV download [verified: main.py:1438 same pattern on completions CSV export, allowing bulk cross-region export of customer/job completion PII.]

Region-scoping bypass on incidents CSV export for unset-region dispatchers — Bulk cross-region export of internal incident notes and customer PII via CSV download [verified: main.py:1473 same pattern on incidents CSV export, which also serializes internal_notes (line 1486), leaking internal notes and PII across all regions.]

Sensitive Authorization header written to logs — Credential/token leakage to anyone with log access, enabling session/account takeover [verified: The raw Authorization header value is logged verbatim at warning level alongside the full body, exposing bearer credentials to anyone with log access.]

Open redirect via unvalidated lane parameter — Phishing via a trusted-domain redirect to attacker-controlled sites [verified: `lane` is passed straight into RedirectResponse with no allow-list or same-origin check, enabling open redirect to attacker-controlled hosts.]

Reflected XSS via |safe-rendered user input — Reflected cross-site scripting allowing session/cookie theft or actions in the victim's browser context [verified: Template explicitly disables autoescaping via `|safe` on the raw `card` parameter and returns it as HTMLResponse, so injected script executes in the browser.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of a logged-in victim and read the response [verified: The Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while Allow-Credentials is set true, which is the textbook CORS misconfiguration allowing any origin credentialed access.]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized MongoDB filter — Bypass query logic or execute server-side JavaScript via $where operator [verified: The JSON body's `filter`/whole payload is passed unvalidated as the MongoDB query dict to find_one, permitting operator injection (e.g. $where) with no schema/type validation.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept or tamper with outbound HTTPS traffic [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is explicitly built and used for the outbound HTTPS request, disabling certificate validation and enabling MITM.]

Region-scoping bypass on worker listing for unset-region dispatchers — Cross-region disclosure of worker roster/PII to a dispatcher who should be scoped to a single region [verified: main.py:597 same pattern on worker listing; unset-region dispatcher bypasses filter and lists all workers company-wide.]

Region-scoping bypass on service-location listing for unset-region dispatchers — Cross-region disclosure of customer service locations/addresses to an under-scoped dispatcher [verified: main.py:608 same pattern on service-locations query; filter never applied when region_id is None, exposing all customer addresses.]

Region-scoping bypass on route listing for unset-region dispatchers — Cross-region disclosure of route schedules and worker assignments [verified: main.py:1134 same pattern on route listing; unset-region dispatcher retrieves all regions' routes and worker assignments.]

CSV formula injection via customer-controlled company_name in exports — Formula injection in spreadsheet exports opened by dispatchers/admins can lead to code execution (legacy Excel DDE), credential/data exfiltration, or compromise of privileged staff workstations. [verified: company_name is fully attacker-controlled at registration (main.py:458) and flows unescaped into csv_response (main.py:1377-1388) used by routes/completions exports.]

CSV formula injection via customer-controlled incident summary in incidents export — A malicious customer can plant spreadsheet formulas that execute or leak data when staff open the incidents export. [verified: customer_summary is not stripped for the customer role (only internal_notes is, main.py:1067) and is written unescaped into incidents.csv via the same csv_response sink.]

Internal notes disclosed via external API-key integration endpoint — Any holder of a valid (even region-scoped) integration API key can read internal_notes on jobs, exposing internal-only operational/customer information to external systems [verified: job_out includes internal_notes whenever user is None (main.py:348), and integration_status_update passes user=None with shallow=True (main.py:1688), so any valid API key holder receives internal_notes with no role check preventing it.]

Unvalidated X-Forwarded-For trusted for audit log IP address — Attackers can forge the source IP recorded in the audit trail for their own malicious actions, undermining audit log integrity/forensics [verified: client_ip() (main.py:91-95) takes X-Forwarded-For verbatim with no trusted-proxy check and audit() writes it straight into ip_address, so any caller can forge the audit-log IP for their own actions.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag on registration — Session cookie can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, enabling session hijacking via network interception [verified: register() hardcodes secure=False (main.py:493) while login() derives it from COOKIE_SECURE (main.py:428), so self-registered sessions lack the Secure flag even when the deployment sets COOKIE_SECURE=true.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag on registration path — Session cookie can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP and intercepted by a network attacker (e.g. on shared Wi-Fi or via SSL-stripping), enabling session hijacking for newly registered accounts even when the deployment is otherwise configured to require secure cookies. [verified: Confirmed duplicate of idx 2/7: register()'s cookie ignores COOKIE_SECURE entirely, unlike login().]
